author: BBC News
description:
Five men have been arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act and explosive offences after three suspicious vehicles were reported near RAF Fairford airbase in Gloucestershire, England.

A major incident was declared and dozens of homes near the facility were evacuated.  The base is used by US bombers carrying out airstrikes against Iran. 

An Army explosive ordnance disposal team examined vehicles near the base, with counter-terror police leading the investigation.

President Donald Trump said those arrested had been "looking to do big damage", adding: "We had them under view for a long time, and we got them."  

The US Department of Defense raised the threat level at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk - which hosts the USAF's 48th Fighter Wing - to its second-highest category.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he had been in contact with his US counterpart, Pete Hegseth.

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Simon Jones and James Landale.

description:
Today, we look at Andy Burnham’s plans for a national care service for England.

In the prime minister’s first Sunday morning interview of his tenure, he told Laura that he would connect the care system to the NHS, and make it free at the point of use, but not before the next General Election.

Laura, Paddy, and Joe Pike look at how it would work and how much it would cost.

They also talk through other interesting things to come out of the conversation, including Burnham’s refusal to commit to bringing the welfare bill down, and support for a third runway at Heathrow.

author: BBC News
description:
Five men have been arrested and remain in custody as counter-terrorism police investigate a major incident near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, UK.

The men were initially arrested on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and were later further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act. Gloucestershire Police said officers received a report of three suspicious vehicles travelling towards the RAF base at about 00:45 BST.

Around 85 homes have been evacuated in nearby Whelford while investigations continue. Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone said work to establish the full nature of the incident is ongoing.
 
A British Army bomb disposal team is carrying out operations at the scene, with aerial footage showing robots deployed to examine vehicles.
 
RAF Fairford has long been used as a forward operating location by the US military. The US Air Force said it remains vigilant following the incident.

Several men have been arrested on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act, Gloucestershire police said. An army explosive ordnance disposal team is currently examining a number of vehicles.
 
Whitehall officials say the investigation into the incident is being led by counter-terror police.
 
The base has been recently used to deploy American bombers since the country's conflict in Iran began on 28 February.
